chapter: Central Problems and the Production Possibility Curve
trick: Read the position of the point and the whole answer follows: on the curve is full and efficient use, inside means something is idle, outside is impossible today. The curve bows outward because resources are not equally good at both jobs, so each extra unit costs more than the last.

video.query: production possibility curve central problems class 11 economics

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the production possibility curve.

items.statement: A point inside the curve means resources are unemployed or used inefficiently.
items.why: The economy could have more of both goods without giving up either, so something is being wasted.

items.statement: A point outside the curve can be reached if people simply work harder.
items.why: It is unattainable with today's resources and technology. Only growth in resources or better technology moves the curve outward.

items.statement: The curve slopes downward because producing more of one good means producing less of the other.
items.why: Resources are fully used, so the only way to get more of one is to move resources away from the other. That sacrifice is the opportunity cost.

items.statement: Opportunity cost is the money price of the good.
items.why: It is the next best alternative given up, measured in goods, not in rupees. A student choosing Arts gives up the Science seat, whatever the fees.

items.statement: Every point on the curve is equally desirable.
items.why: All of them are efficient, but choosing between guns and butter is a social judgement, not a technical one.

trick: Ask one question and the system names itself: who decides what gets produced? The price mechanism alone is capitalist, the government alone is socialist, both together is mixed. India is mixed, which is why the answer to 'what kind of economy is India' is never 'socialist'.

trick: Marginal utility falls as you consume more, but total utility is still rising the whole time marginal utility stays positive. Total utility peaks exactly where marginal utility hits zero — that single sentence answers most questions in this chapter.

video.query: law of diminishing marginal utility total and marginal utility class 11

data.prompt: Work through a utility schedule one step at a time.
data.problem: A consumer's total utility from eating rasgullas is: 1st → 20 units, 2nd → 35, 3rd → 45, 4th → 50, 5th → 50, 6th → 45.

steps.ask: What is the marginal utility of the 2nd rasgulla?
steps.why: Marginal utility is the change in total utility: 35 − 20 = 15.

steps.ask: What is the marginal utility of the 5th?
At which rasgulla is total utility highest?
steps.why: Total utility reaches 50 at the 4th and stays there at the 5th, which is where marginal utility is zero.

steps.ask: What does the 6th rasgulla tell you?
steps.why: Total utility falls from 50 to 45, so the 6th unit has a marginal utility of −5. Eating past satisfaction causes discomfort.

data.answer: Marginal utility falls throughout, reaches zero at the 5th unit where total utility peaks at 50, and turns negative after that.

trick: Domestic means inside the borders whoever earns it; National means earned by residents wherever they are. So National = Domestic + net factor income from abroad. And 'gross' minus depreciation is 'net' — those two words are the only difference between four of the aggregates.

video.query: GDP GNP NDP NNP national income aggregates class 11 economics

data.prompt: Match each aggregate with what it means.

pairs.right: Value of final goods produced inside the country in a year, before depreciation
GDP at market price minus depreciation
GDP plus net factor income from abroad
NNP at factor cost — what residents actually earn
The fall in value of capital through wear and tear
Income earned by residents abroad minus income earned by foreigners here

chapter: Money, Banking and the Reserve Bank of India
trick: The RBI does the things no ordinary bank may do: it issues currency, keeps the government's account and lends to other banks. A commercial bank accepts deposits and lends to the public. Every 'function of the central bank' question is really asking you to spot which of those two lists an item belongs to.

items.label: Accepts savings deposits from the public
Acts as banker to the government
Is the lender of last resort
Controls credit through the repo rate and CRR
Keeps the country's foreign exchange reserves

trick: Demand-pull is too much money chasing too few goods; cost-push is production itself becoming dearer. And unemployment has a type for each cause: seasonal follows the calendar, frictional is the gap between two jobs, structural is a skill the economy no longer wants, disguised is extra hands adding nothing.
